English: That is **my father's** car.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The genitive says whose. It follows the noun it belongs to; der-words take des or -es and add -s to the noun.

English: The name **of the street** is long.
note — the bold part is what the card te: die-words take der in the genitive, and the noun stays the same.

English: The end **of the film** was sad.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Film → des Films: the article and the noun both mark it.

English: At the beginning **of the year** I worked a lot.
German: Am Anfang **des Jahres** habe ich viel gearbeitet.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Short words often take -es: des Jahres.

English: At the end **of the month** I have no money.
German: Am Ende **des Monats** habe ich kein Geld.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Monat → des Monats.

English: **In the middle of the week** the cinema is cheap.
German: Mitte **der Woche** ist das Kino billig.
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Woche → der Woche. Mitte der Woche: midweek.

English: The price **of the ticket** is high.
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Fahrkarte → der Fahrkarte.

English: What is the address **of the hotel**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: das Hotel → des Hotels: das-words take des too.

English: Do you have the number **of the doctor**? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: After -t, the -es is easier to say: des Arztes.

English: **My sister's** flat is big.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Possessives take ein's endings: meiner for a die-word. German puts the owner after the thing.

English: I like the colour **of the car**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: das Auto → des Autos.

English: What is the title **of the book**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: das Buch → des Buches.

English: That is **the colleague's** car.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Kollege takes -n, not -s: des Kollegen.

English: That is **his brother's** friend.
note — the bold part is what the card te: sein → seines, Bruder → Bruders.

English: The mother **of a friend** is a teacher.
note — the bold part is what the card te: ein → eines, Freund → Freundes.

English: **The children's** room is small.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The plural genitive is der, and the noun keeps its plural form.

English: **My parents'** house is old.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Plural: meiner Eltern.

English: The door **of the old** house is broken.
German: Die Tür **des alten** Hauses ist kaputt.
note — the bold part is what the card te: After des, the adjective takes -en: des alten Hauses.

English: Berlin is the capital **of Germany**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: A name without an article just adds -s in the genitive: Deutschlands.

English: **Whose** bag is that?
note — the bold part is what the card te: wessen: whose. In speech, Wem gehört die Tasche? is more common.

English: Because of **the rain** we're staying at home.
German: Wegen **des Regens** bleiben wir zu Hause.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wegen takes the genitive: des Regens.

English: Because of **the traffic jam** I'm late.
German: Wegen **des Staus** komme ich zu spät.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Stau → des Staus. zu spät: too late.

English: Because of **the strike** there are no trains running.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Streik → des Streiks.

English: Because of **the noise** I can't sleep.
German: Wegen **des Lärms** kann ich nicht schlafen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Lärm → des Lärms.

English: Because of **the delay** we arrived late.
German: Wegen **der Verspätung** sind wir spät angekommen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Verspätung → der Verspätung.

English: Because of **my illness** I couldn't come.
German: Wegen **meiner Krankheit** konnte ich nicht kommen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Krankheit → meiner Krankheit.

English: Because of **the weather** we didn't go hiking.
German: Wegen **des Wetters** sind wir nicht gewandert.
note — the bold part is what the card te: das Wetter → des Wetters.

English: Because of **the exam** I'm studying a lot.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wegen der Prüfung takes the first place; the verb follows.

English: Because of **the price** I'm not buying the jacket.
German: Wegen **des Preises** kaufe ich die Jacke nicht.
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Preis → des Preises: -es after s.
